description:
Free. Unlimited. Automatic. AutoMiles logs and sorts every drive for you — with no 40-drive monthly cap, no subscription, and no paywall.

Most mileage trackers stop you at around 40 automatic drives a month, then ask for $60 or more a year. AutoMiles is different: unlimited automatic trips, free.

New — fewer ways to miss a drive
AutoMiles now spots the start of a drive from the low-power location it keeps while your car is parked, so a drive that begins after the app has been closed for a while is less likely to be missed.

Easier on your battery
A mileage tracker is parked far more of the day than it is driving, so AutoMiles now eases off the GPS while your car is sitting still and switches to full accuracy only once you are actually moving. Your drives are recorded exactly as before — the app simply stops working so hard in between.

A deduction that follows the real IRS rate
2026 is a split year: the IRS standard mileage rate is 72.5 cents through 30 June and 76 cents from 1 July. AutoMiles prices every business mile against the rate that was in force on the day you drove it, so the second half of the year is not quietly under-counted. Your dashboard leads with the number that matters — your estimated deduction — for this month or the whole tax year.

Driving abroad or filing elsewhere? Settings has a tax region picker — United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, or your own custom rate and currency — and the app detects your region on first run.

Free and unlimit
releaseNotes:
Walks are no longer mistaken for drives. Recording now starts only on real driving signals: a vehicle reading must come with driving speed, one stray GPS speed spike is ignored, and walking away from your parked car no longer begins a new trip.

Also fixed: a background-tracking crash on Android 12+ that could stop drive detection until the app was reopened, and the Android notification could claim a drive was being recorded while AutoMiles was only watching.
